phone.sources.already: What already went across stays on your computer. To delete it, use {fromYourPhones} there.
phone.calendar.label: Your calendar
phone.calendar.why.title: Bring your calendar to your computer?
phone.calendar.why.what: Nocturne reads what’s in this phone’s calendar: each appointment’s title, time, place and who’s invited, from two days ago to two weeks ahead.
phone.calendar.why.where: It goes only to your computer, the same way as everything this phone keeps: in locked messages only your computer can open. Nocturne has no account and keeps nothing anywhere else.
phone.calendar.why.for: Your page shows what’s on today and this week, and Ask can answer “When is the dentist?” Each line shows which calendar it came from.
phone.calendar.why.never: Nocturne never adds, changes or deletes anything in your calendar.
phone.calendar.why.next: Next, your phone asks if Nocturne may see your calendar.
phone.calendar.refused.title: Your calendar stays on this phone.
phone.calendar.refused.body: Nocturne works just the same without it. You can bring it later in {thisPhone}.
phone.calendar.bring.hint: Two days back to two weeks ahead, read only.
phone.calendar.which.note: Holidays and birthdays start off, because they fill the page without saying much.
phone.calendar.notes.hint: Usually call links and dial-in numbers. Off keeps your page tidy.
phone.calendar.lastSent: Last sent {time} · {count, plural, one {# appointment} other {# appointments}}
phone.calendar.stoppedOnComputer.title: Your computer isn’t taking your calendar from this phone.
phone.calendar.stoppedOnComputer.body: Turn it back on there, under {fromYourPhones}.
phone.calendar.off.title: Calendar is off in your phone’s settings.
phone.calendar.off.body: Nothing is read until you turn it back on there.
phone.calendar.tooMany: Too many to bring at once. Choose fewer calendars.
phone.health.label: Health
phone.health.why.title: Bring health readings to your computer?
phone.health.why.what: Nocturne reads the kinds you choose from Health Connect: sleep, heart rate, resting heart rate, blood pressure, steps and workouts.
phone.health.why.far: From the last 30 days, then each new reading.
phone.health.why.where: Only to your computer, in locked messages only your computer can open. Nocturne has no account and keeps nothing anywhere else.
phone.health.why.for: Your journal shows how you slept and moved beside what you wrote, and your page can show last night’s sleep.
phone.health.why.never: Nocturne never adds or changes anything in Health. It can’t tell what your numbers mean for your health. A doctor or nurse can.
phone.health.why.next: Next, choose which kinds. Then your phone asks you to confirm.
phone.health.kind.sleep.hint: Beside your morning check-in, and on your page.
phone.health.kind.heartRate.hint: The day’s range, beside your journal.
phone.health.kind.restingHeartRate.hint: One number a day, as a line over the weeks.
phone.health.kind.bloodPressure.hint: Your readings by day, if you measure at home.
phone.health.kind.steps.hint: How much you moved each day.
phone.health.kind.workout.hint: Walks, runs and swims on your day’s timeline.
phone.health.kind.weight.hint: A line over the months. Never on your page.
phone.health.kinds.title: Which kinds
phone.health.kinds.foot: You can change these any time in {thisPhone}.
phone.health.done.title: Bringing {kinds}.
phone.health.done.body: Readings show on your computer as they go across. The first 30 days can take a minute.
phone.health.none.title: Health stays on this phone.
phone.health.none.body: Nocturne works just the same without it. You can bring it later in {thisPhone}.
phone.health.missing.title: Health Connect is needed
phone.health.missing.body: On this phone, health readings come through Health Connect, Google’s free app. Get it, then come back here.
phone.health.older.hint: Up to a year back, where your phone has them.
phone.health.lastSent: Last sent {time} · {count, plural, one {# reading} other {# readings}}
phone.health.fixed: Nocturne can’t tell what your numbers mean for your health. A doctor or nurse can.
phone.health.takenBack.title: Health is off in Health Connect.
phone.health.takenBack.body: Nothing is read until you turn it back on there.
phone.rationale.title: How Nocturne uses your health readings
phone.rationale.what: Nocturne reads only the kinds you allow: sleep, heart rate, resting heart rate, blood pressure, steps, workouts and, if you turn it on, weight. It never writes to Health Connect.
phone.rationale.why: To show your readings beside your journal and last night’s sleep on your morning page, on your own computer.
phone.rationale.where: Readings go only to the computer you paired, in locked messages only it can open. Nobody else receives them, including the people who make Nocturne. Nocturne has no account, no ads and no analytics.
phone.rationale.keeping: Your computer keeps readings until you delete them there.
phone.rationale.stopping: Turn Health off in Nocturne’s {thisPhone}, or take the permission back in Health Connect. To delete what went across, use {fromYourPhones} on your computer.
